findings.claim: Examiner reports highlight that many students confuse binary multiples with decimal SI prefixes (kB, MB, GB, TB, which use 1000-based steps) or cannot state how many bytes are in a tebibyte.
findings.truth: The underlying point is right, but no examiner report is cited or verifiable. Attributing the claim to examiner reports invents a source. State it as a common error instead.
findings.evidence: House rule on fabricated examiner claims; spec 2.3.1 lists only the binary multiples (bit, nibble, byte, kibibyte, mebibyte, gibibyte, tebibyte)

findings.claim: The examiner specifically awards marks for the correct unit abbreviation.
findings.truth: A separate mark for the unit abbreviation is invented. The true advice is simply to write the unit with the answer, because a bare number does not answer the question.
findings.evidence: Spec assessment section (lines 706-725) states paper structure and item types only; no mark-scheme rule of this kind exists

findings.claim: (3) Not stating 'pixels' as the unit for width and height - this is a marking point in its own right.
findings.truth: Labelling width and height as pixels is not a separate marking point. The real common error in a file-size calculation is dividing bits by 1,000 instead of 8.
findings.evidence: House rule on fabricated examiner claims; recomputation of the worked example (640 x 480 x 24 = 7,372,800 bits; / 8 = 921,600 bytes)

findings.claim: A memory chip with address lines can access 2^10 = 1,024 locations, not 1,000.
findings.truth: The number of address lines is missing, so the sentence does not say why the answer is 1,024. It needs 10 address lines to reach 2^10 locations.

findings.claim: For hex conversion, the command word will often be 'Convert' (2 marks) - show the nibble split and both hex digits to secure full marks.
findings.truth: The tariff is asserted without a source. The spec fixes only the paper total (75 marks, five questions, one per topic); it sets no tariff for a named command word. The claim is hedged and plausible, so it is recorded rather than edited.

findings.claim: Two-mark 'Define' and 'State' questions carry a four-tier band ladder (Mastering / Secure / Developing / Emerging) - lesson 2 question 2 and lesson 4 question 4.
findings.truth: Edexcel point-marks short items of this size; a band ladder belongs to extended-open-response items only. This is the band-ladder queue item in the retro programme, so it is recorded here rather than edited piecemeal.
findings.evidence: spec lines 706-725: the paper mixes multiple-choice, short-, medium- and extended-open-response items

summary: Every calculation in the unit was recomputed and all of it is correct: binary/denary/hex conversions, two's complement negation and the -128 to +127 range, the addition worked example and both overflow cases, logical versus arithmetic right shifts (including sign-bit fill), all image and sound file sizes, and every KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB conversion. All 20 knowledge-check answer keys, all 3 match orders and all 46 flashcard answers are right, and the storage units match the spec's binary multiples exactly. The only defects are four fabricated or incomplete exam-technique claims; no HIGH findings.
